source_evidence: Because many ETFs buy and sell portfolio securities in in-kind exchange (rather than for cash), they typically have fewer capital gains distributions – and thus lower taxes – than mutual funds.
answer: ETF tax efficiency can come from how the fund handles portfolio securities. Many ETFs use in-kind exchanges rather than selling securities for cash, which typically results in fewer capital gains distributions and lower taxes than mutual funds. This is a general tendency, not a guarantee that every ETF will have lower taxes.
